claims.text: High-strain-rate loading dynamically stabilizes intrinsic lattice distortions and local chemical order in single-phase high-entropy alloys.
Intrinsic lattice distortions and local chemical order are features of the proposed single-phase HEA initial state.
Dynamic stabilization of intrinsic lattice distortions hinders dislocation glide.
Dynamic stabilization of intrinsic lattice distortions promotes dislocation entanglement.
The proposed restriction of dislocation motion produces high yield strength in the HEA.
The proposed dislocation mechanism produces an unusual combination of high strength and ductility.
The strength-ductility synergy attributed to dynamically stabilized lattice distortions and local chemical order is absent in conventional alloys lacking those features.
Conventional alloys lacking significant lattice distortions exhibit faster dislocation motion than the HEA.
Conventional alloys lacking significant lattice distortions exhibit lower strain hardening than the HEA.
Under high-strain-rate deformation, the HEA will have higher yield strength than the conventional-alloy baseline.
Under high-strain-rate deformation, the HEA will have a higher strain-hardening rate than the conventional-alloy baseline.
Under high-strain-rate deformation, the HEA will have greater ductility than the conventional-alloy baseline.
In situ measurements will show lattice-strain evolution in the HEA that is distinct from that of the conventional baseline.
In situ measurements will show reduced dislocation mobility in the HEA relative to the conventional baseline.
The proposed mechanism operates during high-strain-rate elastic-plastic deformation from room temperature to moderately elevated temperatures.
Thermally activated deformation mechanisms remain active over the proposed strain-rate and temperature range.
Intrinsic lattice distortions can be maintained over the proposed temperature range but may be overridden by stronger thermal effects outside it.
Prior evidence links local chemical order and lattice-related heterogeneity in entropy alloys to mechanical performance.
The relative contribution of the proposed mechanism across strain rates and temperatures remains unquantified.

Comparable lattice-distortion evolution, dislocation resistance, and strain-hardening improvement in the conventional control would falsify the claim that dynamic lattice-distortion stabilization is the primary HEA mechanism.
